title: Introduce operator session authz checkpoint and KMS consent debouncer with audit compactor
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add operator session authorization checkpointing middleware; introduce KMS consent debouncer to reduce redundant remote attest calls; add audit compactor to batch high-frequency audit events without losing per-request integrity.
body:
Summary: This PR introduces three coordinated changes aimed at reducing operator impersonation risks, cutting noisy KMS attestation traffic, and improving downstream audit ingestion efficiency. The core pieces are: (1) operator-session-authz-checkpoint middleware which binds operator actions to session-scoped claims and enforces a checksum during cross-service calls; (2) kms-consent-debouncer service-side cache that coalesces repeated consent checks for the same operator-session/KMS-resource tuple for a short TTL to reduce backend KMS QPS; (3) audit-compactor which batches audit events produced by high-throughput endpoints into compact envelopes while preserving per-request assertions and per-tenant ordering.
Motivation and context: We observed two recent incidents where long-lived operator sessions allowed stale operator tokens to be replayed across services (SUP-9312). Additionally, KMS metrics showed spiky consent calls from operator tooling workflows resulting in throttling. Finally, downstream audit-collector ingestion was overwhelmed by per-token audit items from high-frequency paths. These changes together reduce attack surface, smooth KMS load, and make audit ingestion more robust.
Design highlights: - Operator session checkpointing: a lightweight middleware placed at the operator gateway and replicated at internal operator-facing services. On request ingress it attaches a session-checksum header derived from session id, nonce, and service fingerprint. Downstream services validate the checksum before accepting operator-privileged actions. Checksum algorithm is HMAC-SHA256 using a service-local key persisted in operator keystore. - KMS consent debouncer: short-lived (2s default) in-memory debouncing keyed by (operator-session-id, kms-key-id, action). When identical consent checks happen within the TTL we return the cached decision result (and re-check asynchronously when a miss occurs). The implementation uses the existing token service cache with an opt-in feature flag per service. - Audit compactor: a streaming compaction layer in the audit forwarder that groups events by tenant and route within a time window (100ms default) into an envelope. Each envelope contains the minimal per-event assertions required for compliance (timestamp, tenant-id, operator-session-id, event-hash). Full per-event payloads remain available in the envelope for rehydration by downstream processors.
Backward compatibility: Feature flags gate both the debouncer and compactor; operator-session checkpointing can be enabled progressively by rollout at gateways and then gradual rollout in internal services.
Rollout plan: 1) Deploy middleware in gateway in opt-in mode and enable feature flag for 5% traffic; 2) Enable KMS debouncer behind feature flag for operator tooling endpoints; 3) Enable audit compactor on audit-forwarder with dry-run mode for 48h; 4) Ramp to 100% if no regressions.
Testing and validation: - Unit tests for checksum computation and validation, plus negative tests for tampered headers. - Integration tests with operator-gateway -> service flow exercising checksum enforcement. - Load tests showing KMS consent QPS reduction in synthetic operator workflows (~55% reduction in consent calls for a sampled scenario). - End-to-end audit ingestion smoke tests to verify envelope format and rehydration path.
Security review notes: HMAC key rotation handled by keystore manager; middleware tolerates key rollover with dual-key signature acceptance during transition window. Consent cache TTL default errs on the conservative side (2s) and can be tuned per-customer. Audit fidelity is preserved: every event retains an event-hash and rehydration path.
Observability: New metrics added: authz.checkpoint.validations_total, authz.checkpoint.failures_total, kms.debouncer.hits, kms.debouncer.misses, audit.compactor.envelopes_emitted, audit.compactor.rehydrations. Tracing includes a new span 'authz.checkpoint' with decision tag.
Backout/rollback: feature flags and per-service config allow immediate disable. If checksum validation failures spike, the middleware has a soft-fail mode that only emits telemetry but allows the request for 10 minutes while we roll back.
Related work: builds on ENG-5421 (operator-session model) and complements ENG-5480 (audit forwarder improvements). See SUP-9312 for incident context.
